newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Taiwan-HK official contact needs okay.
newsitem.headline: China says Taiwan-HK official contact needs okay.

text.p: Beijing said on Thursday any official contact or exchanges between rival Taiwan and China's new territory of Hong Kong needed the approval of the central government.

"Official contact, exchanges, negotiations, signing of agreements between the Hong Kong Special Adminstrative Region and the Taiwan region must be reported to the central government for approval," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang.

Relations between Hong Kong and Taiwan should respect the one China principle and should not create "two Chinas, one Taiwan or Taiwan independence", Tang said, referring to Beijing's concerns that Taiwan may abandon its avowed goal of reunification and declare independence.
The "one country, two systems" formula was workable in Hong Kong and Macau and was also workable in Taiwan, he said. Portuguese-run Macau is due to return to Chinese rule in December 1999.
Reunification with Taiwan would be realised regardless of the difficulties, Tang said.
He shrugged off protests this week by democrats in Hong Kong against the inauguration of a new Beijing-anointed legislature, saying "unharmonious sounds... do not win the people's hearts".
